candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of critical low flow (Qa = 0) and the resulting dilution factor (CD = 100%) could change which derived numeric effluent limits are considered applicable when comparing reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span:
The reasonable potential calculation was performed using test results for those parameters (tested
at MQL) that were greater than the MQL. Detection limit values were used for those parameters
reported as non-detect whose values are above the MQL. For RP calculation purpose, averaged
value of data set is utilized in the RP calculations. See the RP spreadsheet of the fact sheet
(attached).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of how MQL exceedances, non-detects above MQL, and averaged versus other aggregation methods are applied in RP calculations could change whether numeric limits are established versus monitoring-only, and how non-numeric or below-MQL results are treated in compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span:
However, effluent data for Total Recoverable Cyanide 6.28 ug/L (Estimated or J, 5/20/2020) and
(ND < MDL of 2.96 ug/L, which was below the MQL of 10 ug/L, 5/26/21), and (ND <RDL of
0.005 mg/L), with a geometric mean of 2.854 ug/L The limiting Wildlife Habitat and Chronic
Aquatic Criteria is 5.2 ug/L. As a result, the draft permit establishes monitoring requirements for
Total Recoverable Cyanide to obtain more data for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the J-flagged estimate, multiple non-detect qualifiers (MDL, MQL, RDL), geometric mean versus the 5.2 ug/L criterion, and the statement that only monitoring requirements (not numeric limits) are established could change applicable limit selection, whether monitoring is required versus a numeric compliance comparison, and how missing or qualified results are classified.

candidates.exact_span:
The effluent data for delta-BHC were 0.00245 ug/L (5/20/2020), ND <0.002 ug/L (5/26/2021)
and ND <0.002 ug/L (6/2/2021) with a geometric mean of 0.0013481 ug/L. NMWQS does not
have numeric criteria for delta-BHC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reported values and non-detects are treated as usable measurements and whether the absence of NMWQS numeric criteria means no enforceable limit applies could change limit-applicability determinations and the semantic classification of ND results.

candidates.exact_span:
However, there
is insufficient information in the ECOTOX database to calculate delta-BHC chronic aquatic life
criterion for a particular species, genus or group that is representative of the form of life to be
preserved in New Mexico, using the results of toxicological studies published in scientific
journals available from EPA's ECOTOX database.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this insufficiency is read as precluding any derived numeric limit for delta-BHC affects whether an enforceable numeric discharge limit can be assigned versus report-only or unresolved status.

candidates.exact_span:
EPA proposes additional delta-BHC monitoring in the effluent to be used in the next permit
cycle should there be sufficient toxicological studies at that time to calculate limitations. As a
result, the permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source
water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for
approval. The plan must also include any use of delta-BHC at the facility, if any. Once approved,
the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more
frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit. The results of this study shall be
attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Timing conditions (six months after effective date; years 2–5 only; quarterly or more frequent), plan-approval prerequisites, intake versus effluent sampling, and DMR attachment requirements could change which monitoring obligations apply in FY2025 and how missing or study-attached results are classified.
